Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Alex Park (Redwood CSM), Maya Thompson (Harbor ML), Ethan Cole (Harbor VP Eng), Sofia Rivera (Harbor Sec), Luis Ortega (Harbor Platform)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'll kick things off, happy to be here.
[00:12] Maya Thompson: Hi Jordan, thanks, Maya here. We're excited to get started.
[00:15] Ethan Cole: Ethan, hi.
[00:17] Sofia Rivera: Sofia here. We'll mostly be focusing on the security bits but want to hear the plan.
[00:24] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Quick agenda — intros, goals, architecture options (hosted API vs dedicated vs private VPC), security requirements, pilot scope and timelines, and then next steps.
[00:36] Priya Menon: Hi all, Priya on the SE side. I'll be owning the perf work and helping with integration patterns.
[00:42] Alex Park: Alex from CS, I'll schedule check-ins and make sure success criteria are tracked.
[00:48] Maya Thompson: For context, our goals are: 1) replace an in-house reranker for clinical triage, 2) keep p95 under 300ms for endpoint calls where feasible, 3) data must never leave our EU region, and 4) SOC2 compliance and auditability.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Great, noted. Can you share current stack? latency and volume?
[01:12] Maya Thompson: We're on GCP with k8s, using a microservice that calls our in-house LLM for reranking. Traffic for the first pilot will be ~5 TPS, peak 15 TPS. Token sizes vary, average payload small — about 80 tokens per request.
[01:29] Ethan Cole: Also want to flag budget sensitivity. We'd prefer hosted if it meets security and residency, but if costs balloon, dedicated or self-hosted paths might be better.
[01:43] Jordan Lee: Understood. We'll outline tradeoffs. For EU residency, Redwood Private (VPC) is typical; we also have Dedicated capacity in region, and hosted with data controls for short-term trial.
[01:56] Sofia Rivera: On the security side we need KMS integration, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, retention controls, and an SOC2 report. Also, any egress endpoints need to be limited.
[02:09] Priya Menon: We support KMS integrations on Private and Dedicated, and hosted can be accompanied by contractual terms for data handling, but keys are customer-managed only on Private. Audit logs and RBAC are available in the Console; I can send screenshots.
[02:25] Jordan Lee: I'll attach our security pack afterward. It includes SOC2, ISO, pen test summaries, and KMS options.
[02:32] Maya Thompson: Good. On latency — Priya, are you able to do a baseline perf run against our dev dataset?
[02:38] Priya Menon: Yes. Could you drop a small sample (1000 rows) and a representative prompt? I'll run both hosted and our dedicated profile to show delta.
[02:48] Luis Ortega: We can provision a dev VPC and firewall rules; what IPs do you need?
[02:53] Priya Menon: I'll share exact egress IP CIDR for the test. For Private deployment we'll need connectivity details and possibly a VPN or direct connect.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: Quick Q on timeline — Maya, when do you want pilot live?
[03:06] Maya Thompson: We'd like a pilot in two weeks if possible. That gives us time to finish security review and run perf.
[03:12] Alex Park: We'll aim for 2 weeks. I'll put together a milestone plan after this call.
[03:18] Sofia Rivera: On the security questionnaire — we did send an initial one, but there are a few outstanding items about key rotation and audit retention.
[03:27] Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll fill those specifics and add the retention SLAs.
[03:31] --- Transcript jump (typical in auto transcripts; filler removed) ---
[04:00] Ethan Cole: For integration, do you offer both REST API and SDKs? Our service is Java/Kotlin.
[04:06] Priya Menon: Yes, REST and language SDKs. Kotlin/Java will typically call the REST endpoint; we can provide a small client snippet.
[04:14] Maya Thompson: Is there a webhook for async responses? Some rerank work can be batched offline.
[04:19] Priya Menon: We have streaming responses and webhook-like callbacks for async jobs in Dedicated setups; for hosted, you'd poll or use streaming. I'll share patterns.
[04:28] Luis Ortega: About batch — any recommended batching settings for short prompts to keep latency low?
[04:33] Priya Menon: For low-latency small prompts, keep batching small and use prefix caching where you can. We'll recommend batching/window settings after seeing distribution.
[04:44] Jordan Lee: Also quantization and model variant tradeoffs — we'll propose a model that keeps p95 under target while being cost-effective.
[04:51] Maya Thompson: We care a lot about hallucination and clinical safety. Is there monitoring or guardrails?
[04:57] Priya Menon: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerting tied to evals and prompt sets. We can onboard your test prompts into the eval suite.
[05:07] Maya Thompson: Great.
[05:12] Sofia Rivera: A couple more security specifics: Do you support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) for hosted?
[05:17] Jordan Lee: BYOK is only on Private deployments at present. For hosted we provide customer agreement options and strict data handling but can't host customer keys.
[05:27] Sofia Rivera: Okay that helps. We'll likely push for Private if we can't get satisfactory contractual assurances.
[05:33] Ethan Cole: On cost — any quick back-of-envelope for 5 TPS at 80 tokens?
[05:38] Jordan Lee: I'll send pricing estimate; rough math: hosted might be X per token and dedicated has a commit; I'll get a concrete number in the follow-up.
[05:48] --- [10:12] --- (jumping ahead) ---
[10:12] Priya Menon: I'm going to outline the benchmark plan: 1) run hosted API with a dev key using a 1k sample, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec; 2) run Dedicated profile simulation in our test harness; 3) test Private if we can spin a small private instance or run a perf sim. I'll record logs and sample traces.
[10:30] Maya Thompson: That sounds good. For the test harness, are we sharing any logs that include PHI?
[10:36] Priya Menon: Please scrub PHI. We'll only accept de-identified or synthetic samples. We can also provide on-prem benchmarks if needed.
[10:44] Luis Ortega: We'll produce de-identified dataset and a synthetic edge case set.
[10:48] Jordan Lee: Excellent.
[11:02] Sofia Rivera: Regarding audit logs, what retention window can you guarantee for Dedicated and Private? We need 1 year retention for our auditors.
[11:11] Priya Menon: Private gives you full control; Dedicated supports configurable retention up to 18 months on request under enterprise SLA. Hosted default is 90 days, but we can negotiate extended retention as an add-on.
[11:26] Sofia Rivera: Good to know. Also, SAML SSO — we need Azure AD integration.
[11:32] Jordan Lee: We support SAML/OAuth; for Private we can integrate directly with your IdP.
[11:38] Ethan Cole: For network, Latency from EU to Redwood hosted region — do you have region options in EU?
[11:44] Priya Menon: Yes, we have EU regions (Frankfurt/Amsterdam). For best latency and data residency we'd recommend deploying in your preferred EU region.
[11:55] Maya Thompson: If we do Private in our cloud, what's the typical deployment time?
[12:01] Priya Menon: Depends on procurement — once infra details are shared, a minimal Private pilot can be provisioned in 1-2 weeks; full production rollouts take longer due to compliance checks.
[12:12] Alex Park: On procurement, Jordan, do we have a standard PO/contract template to send?
[12:16] Jordan Lee: Yes — I'll attach our SOW and standard contract; legal can iterate.
[12:24] --- Slight crosstalk / filler ---
[13:00] Maya Thompson: For success criteria — besides latency, we want accuracy metrics: rerank win rate over baseline at least +8% and no regressions in clinical safety.
[13:12] Priya Menon: We'll instrument evals and create dashboards. Redwood Console can surface per-route token cost and latency and link to specific evals.
[13:23] Ethan Cole: Who's the point for billing?
[13:26] Jordan Lee: Jordan for initial invoice; Alex will be CSM for usage monitoring.
[13:31] Luis Ortega: If we choose Dedicated, what does autoscaling look like?
[13:36] Priya Menon: Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst policies. You can set min and max node pools; we have policies tuned for throughput vs latency.
[13:45] Maya Thompson: Any limits on concurrency per model?
[13:49] Priya Menon: Limits depend on the model and hardware; we'll provide recommended concurrency settings after the perf run.
[14:00] Jordan Lee: Ok let's recap next steps — Priya runs perf tests, Jordan sends security pack and pricing, Sofia returns questionnaire, Alex schedules weekly sync, Luis sends network details.
[14:15] Maya Thompson: That works. Two-week pilot timeline still good.
[14:19] Jordan Lee: Anything else?
[14:22] Sofia Rivera: One last question: how do you handle data deletion requests across logs and caches?
[14:29] Priya Menon: For Private and Dedicated, you control data lifecycles. For hosted we have data deletion procedures and can provide deletion certificates. I'll include details in the security pack.
[14:40] Ethan Cole: Great.
[14:45] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll share the slide deck and security docs. Alex will set up recurring invites.
[14:52] Maya Thompson: Thanks, talk soon.
[14:54] (call ends)
